items.title: Codex plugins patch bugs and verify fixes don't cause regressions
items.summary: Trail of Bits open-sourced two Codex plugins: patching-bugs proves a fix with a three-arm test (fails on the original code, passes on the patch, fails again once reverted), and regression-hunt traces diffs to live repros before an adjudication agent rules on real regressions. Against a baseline Codex agent, regression-hunt cut false positives 25% (95% CI 14-38%) and confirmed 21 regressions across 130+ merged PRs. Engineers can now hand patch and regression checks to agents and get verified evidence instead of a manual diff review. (3 minute read)

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon leads new cybersecurity benchmarks for bug hunting
items.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro for finding vulnerabilities, 54.8% on ExploitGym for exploitation, and 71.0% on CWE-bench for patching. Google says it's twice as likely to generate secure code as predecessor Argon and resisted every evaluated indirect prompt-injection attempt. Access starts limited to a subset of cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program. (3 minute read)

items.title: A smarter scheduler recovers 27% more usable Grace Blackwell GPUs
items.summary: NVL72 racks give full NVLink speed only to jobs that stay on one rack, so node failures and uneven job lengths strand usable GPUs across racks. SkyPilot's topology-aware scheduler and automatic defragmentation recover 27% more usable nodes on a 128-rack, 2,304-node cluster (2,037 vs 1,602) versus naive 18-node slicing, and NVIDIA's GR00T team saw a 14.4% pre-training throughput gain from rack-aware placement alone. Teams running multi-node jobs on Grace Blackwell can reclaim that capacity without buying more racks. (4 minute read)

items.title: Claude Code regularly sends each background agent's transcript to its model
items.summary: Claude Code sends each background agent's full transcript to its model roughly every 30 seconds just to write a 3-5 word status line, with no setting to turn it off since v2.1.232. Independent telemetry in GitHub issue #86879 puts this at 16-26% of a user's total agent spend. Anyone running background agents can now check their own OpenTelemetry query_source field, or apply an unofficial Bun preload script that neutralizes the timer and recovers that spend. (4 minute read)

items.title: A CVSS 10.0 GitLab bug got actively probed against Alpine's own GitLab
items.summary: An attacker spent six days probing CVE-2026-97229, a CVSS 10.0 regex-engine bug in GitLab's CI config parser, against Alpine Linux's own GitLab instance, crashing worker processes 8 times and partially completing the exploit chain 4 times. Alpine's GitLab update didn't close the hole because its container image shipped unpatched upstream Ruby, so it rebuilt the instance from scratch and reset every password. Anyone self-hosting GitLab needs to upgrade Ruby separately, since the fix doesn't ship inside the GitLab update itself. (4 minute read)

items.title: Cloudflare uses OpenAI's Daybreak to investigate its own vulnerabilities
items.summary: Cloudflare uses OpenAI's Daybreak model to investigate vulnerabilities and propose fixes for human review, while its developers use Codex to ship code faster and improve its quality. It's a production example of AI handling the investigation step of vulnerability response, with people still deciding what actually ships. (2 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI's Patch the Planet coordinates fixes for agent-found bugs
items.summary: OpenAI's Patch the Planet connects security researchers, maintainers, and incident responders around critical open-source vulnerabilities that AI agents surface. It's a coordination layer built for turning agent-found bugs into shipped fixes, not just more vulnerability reports. (2 minute read)

items.title: Google's Sleep framework teaches LLMs new facts without forgetting old ones
items.summary: Google Research's Sleep framework alternates a wake phase that stores new information and a sleep phase that consolidates it into a Hope-architecture MoE's long-term parameters, rather than fine-tuning over frozen weights. It held near-zero forgetting when continually translating into unseen languages Manchu and Kalamang, where in-context learning, Cartridges, and SFT all degraded badly, and scaled BABILong recall out to 10M tokens past GPT-4 and Titans. No code has shipped yet, only the arXiv paper. (4 minute read)
